html:
SMTO-FIL-0040 — A piece of the copied file arrived out of order

GUID: 9f0a127d-2ba5-4c40-9048-0701f1ecfcab
Slug: file-transfer-offset-mismatch
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • During a copy between Gateways, the next piece of the file didn't start where the last one ended. SMTO stopped the copy before putting the file in place at the destination.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, use Check connection on both Gateways, and use Check for updates if either is out of date. A dropped connection or a version difference can make a piece arrive twice or skip ahead.
  2. Ask SMTO in the conversation to show the size and last-modified time of the file at the destination and of the original file, and compare them. If the destination file is already there and matches, the copy doesn't need to be repeated.
  3. If the destination file is missing or still the old version, ask SMTO to copy it again. A new copy starts from the beginning instead of continuing the broken one.

What success looks like

  • The new copy finishes and SMTO reports the file was copied and verified.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateways. Don't keep repeating the copy if it fails the same way; the connection between SMTO and the Gateways needs to be checked.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway rejected a source_read or destination_write whose requested offset differed from the session's current accepted byte offset (or exceeded the source size).

What this means

  • A destination_write chunk's requested offset differs from the session's current accepted byte offset. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A destination_write chunk's requested offset differs from the session's current accepted byte offset.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the owned session offset with the last acknowledged chunk; do not assume a lost acknowledgement means bytes were not written.

How to fix it

  • Query destination_status for the transfer_id to read bytes_received, and check both Gateways' logs for a duplicated or retried request (for example after a reconnect) or a controller/Gateway version mismatch. The relay does not resume in place; abort or settle the stage and start a new copy, and never resend chunks at a guessed offset.
  • Inspect the accepted transfer offset and resume from that verified boundary.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Any supported continuation starts exactly at the verified accepted boundary.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors
